What to look for: the two DXC panes and the Clang pane behave differently, and
the point of the link is the wording of the DXC panes, not whether a pane fails.

In both DXC panes, read the single error line. Its subject is the callee
rendered as the LLVM symbol the front end generated for it, not as the HLSL
declaration a few lines above in this source. That is issue 3439. Contrast it
with any front-end diagnostic from the same compiler, which names a function as
written and in quotes; the difference is visible without knowing anything about
DXC internals. The message itself is correct -- the shader really does leave a
declared overload undefined -- so nothing here is a miscompile.

The Clang pane answers a different question, and answers it in an unexpected
way: it succeeds. Scroll its output to the call inside the body of main, then
to the declaration a few lines below it, and note that the callee is declared
and never defined, with no diagnostic of any kind. Read Clang diagnostics
rather than its exit code in general, because its DXIL backend is still
incomplete; the narrower caveat here is that Compiler Explorer runs this pane
in assembly-listing mode rather than producing a validated container, so a
later stage might still object.

The source is a compute restatement of the pixel-shader repro in the issue
body, because Clang's backend cannot lower a pixel shader that writes to a
render target. DXC emits the same message for both spellings; the pixel version
as filed is the one measured locally.
